eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Six
subtitle: Lesson 60 · Data Types, Strings, Dates and Modern T-SQL

code:
SELECT ProductSubcategoryID,
       STRING_AGG(Color, ', ') AS ColorsAvailable
FROM Production.Product
WHERE Color IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ProductSubcategoryID;
caption: An aggregate function that returns a joined string, not a number.

code:
SELECT ProductSubcategoryID,
  STRING_AGG(Color, ', ')
    WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Color ASC) AS ColorsAvailable
FROM Production.Product
WHERE Color IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ProductSubcategoryID;
caption: Without it, concatenation order isn't guaranteed.

code:
-- No WHERE Color IS NOT NULL needed --
-- STRING_AGG skips NULL values on its own:
SELECT ProductSubcategoryID,
  STRING_AGG(Color, ', ')
    WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Color ASC) AS ColorsAvailable
FROM Production.Product
GROUP BY ProductSubcategoryID;
caption: Just like SUM or COUNT, NULLs are simply excluded.

subtitle: The reverse operation -- one string, split into rows.
